effects.name: Accordion Height Auto
effects.description: A disclosure group that opens to its natural content height and closes again smoothly with pure CSS: each panel animates grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr, so there is no measuring, no fixed max-height and no JavaScript animation. The chevron turns (or the plus folds into a minus) on the same token easing, and single- or multiple-open behaviour is a param.
accessibility: APG accordion pattern: each header is a button inside an h4 with aria-expanded and aria-controls; each panel is a labelled region.
Enter or Space toggles; Up/Down move between headers (wrapping) and Home/End jump to the first and last.
A closed panel switches to visibility: hidden once its collapse has finished, so collapsed content is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree without cutting the animation short.
State is shown by the icon and by aria-expanded, never by colour alone.
effects.reducedMotion: Panels open and close at once with no height animation and the icon flips without turning; newly opened content fades in over 160 ms.
performance: Support: the 0fr → 1fr grid-track transition animates to the content height in every evergreen browser (Chrome/Edge 107+, Safari 16+, Firefox 66+), closing included. No dependency on interpolate-size or ::details-content, which are newer and not yet everywhere.
It is a layout animation, but confined to one short panel at a time; the content inside only animates opacity and translate.
No JavaScript runs during the animation: React only flips data attributes and aria-expanded.

effects.name: Bar Race Transition
effects.description: Ranked horizontal bars that resize, re-sort and enter or leave the top list as a period stepper advances. Values and the zero-based axis are interpolated together, so bar length is truthful on every frame and labels tick with their bars.
accessibility: Previous, play/pause and next are real buttons; the period is also a native range input (arrow keys step periods).
A live region announces the period and leader after manual steps and when playback ends, not on every autoplay tick.
Every bar carries its rank, name and value as text; the leader is marked by rank and weight as well as colour.
A visually-hidden table lists the full ranking for the current period.
effects.reducedMotion: Play still advances, but each period is swapped in without tweening values or sliding rows; manual stepping is instant.
performance: Bars are scaled and rows translated with transforms only; the track is measured once per resize.
One rAF tween per step, cancelled on pause, interruption and unmount.
All competitors stay mounted and keyed, so enter and exit are opacity/transform changes rather than DOM churn.

effects.name: Blob Morph
effects.description: Seeded organic forms that morph point-for-point on a spring. Every keyframe samples the same angles, so one closed Catmull-Rom path glides between shapes without kinks; the form masks an illustration, an avatar or a solid fill.
accessibility: The shape is a real button: hovering it, focusing it with the keyboard or pressing it picks the next form, and its label names the form that is showing.
Thumbnail buttons (aria-pressed) jump straight to any form; the form counter is a polite live region.
The masked illustration is decorative (aria-hidden) — no information depends on the shape.
Touch taps morph once (hover is ignored for touch, so a tap never skips two forms).
effects.reducedMotion: Idle drift is switched off and the shape no longer morphs: forms swap with a 160 ms cross-fade from a ghost of the previous form.
performance: One SVG path (plus its hairline echo) is rewritten per frame only while a spring is settling or drift is on; the useRafLoop loop stops at rest and pauses offscreen or in a hidden tab.
Shapes are generated once per seed / point-count / wobble change; a frame integrates 6–14 springs in fixed substeps with no layout reads.
The mask is plain SVG — no filters, no canvas.

effects.name: Brush Linked Range
effects.description: Focus + context: an overview strip with a draggable, resizable brush drives a linked detail chart whose domain eases toward the selection. The brush is hand-built so both handles and the window itself are real keyboard sliders.
accessibility: Start handle, end handle and the window are three role="slider" controls with date-based aria-valuetext.
Arrow keys move by one day, Shift+arrow or PageUp/PageDown by a week, Home/End jump to the limits; presets are plain buttons.
The detail chart is role="img" with a generated text summary (range, mean, low, high); the same figures are visible beside it.
Handles have 44 px hit areas; the y-axis always starts at zero and prints its scale, so rescaling is never silent.
effects.reducedMotion: The detail domain snaps to the selection with no easing; dragging and keyboard control are unchanged.
performance: Pointer capture + a single rAF chase loop that stops when the displayed domain reaches the target.
Only the points inside the visible window (plus one neighbour each side) are turned into a path each frame.
The overview path is computed once per size; both charts re-measure via ResizeObserver.

effects.name: Camera Preset Rig
effects.description: A procedural still-life on a plinth with four named camera positions. Choosing a preset glides position and look-at target on a critically damped spring that can be interrupted mid-flight, and the canvas only renders while the camera is moving.
applications: case-study hero with a detail shot
accessibility: Views are a native radio group in a fieldset: Tab reaches it, arrow keys change the view, and the current view is announced as the checked option.
The canvas has an accessible name and a text description of the composition; a line of text under the picture says what the current view shows.
When WebGL is unavailable an SVG drawing of the same still-life is shown, and the radio group still describes each view.
effects.reducedMotion: The camera cuts straight to the chosen preset: one rendered frame, no travel.
performance: frameloop="demand": at rest nothing renders; while gliding each frame requests the next with invalidate() and stops once position and target have settled.
Eight draw calls of primitive geometry; real shadow maps only on quality profiles that allow them, otherwise generated contact-shadow textures.
The generated shadow texture is disposed on unmount; JSX-declared geometry and materials are released by R3F.

effects.name: Command Menu Reveal
effects.description: A ⌘K command palette built on a native modal <dialog>: the backdrop, panel and result rows enter as one WAAPI sequence with a parent→child stagger, results filter with match highlighting, and the exit layers on top of whatever the entrance was doing so it can be dismissed mid-flight.
accessibility: Native <dialog>.showModal(): focus is trapped by the browser, the page behind is inert, Escape closes and focus returns to the trigger.
Combobox + listbox pattern: the input keeps focus while aria-activedescendant tracks the active option; Arrow Up/Down wrap, Home/End jump, Enter runs.
Options are grouped with labelled role="group"; the empty state and the last-run confirmation are announced through polite live regions.
A visible Esc button closes the palette for pointer and touch users; clicking the backdrop does the same.
effects.reducedMotion: The sequence is built with reducedMotion, so backdrop, panel and rows appear in their end state at once and closing is immediate.
performance: Entrance and exit animate opacity and transform only, through createSequence (WAAPI), and are cancelled when the dialog closes or unmounts.
Rows stagger only on open; filtering swaps results without re-animating.
The dialog content is not rendered while closed.

effects.name: CSS Cube Carousel
effects.description: Four content panels on the faces of a prism that turns with transform-style: preserve-3d and a spring sampled into a CSS linear() easing. No WebGL, no animation loop: one transition on one element.
accessibility: Carousel semantics: a labelled region with aria-roledescription="carousel", each face a group named "n of 4: title"; a polite live region announces the new step.
Only the front face is reachable: the other three are inert, so their controls leave the tab order and the accessibility tree.
Previous/next buttons, step dots (aria-current) and Arrow / Home / End keys anywhere inside the carousel; all targets are at least 44 px (dots 28 px).
It never auto-advances, so there is nothing to pause.
effects.reducedMotion: The prism stops turning: the new panel replaces the old one with a 160 ms opacity cross-fade and the tilt is removed.
performance: A single transform transition on the prism element; faces are static compositor layers.
The spring is pre-sampled with springToLinear(), so there is no JavaScript per frame.
Sizes come from container-query units, so the prism depth always matches the face width without measuring.

effects.name: Cursor Follower
effects.description: A dot and a spring ring that trail the native cursor inside one container and read what is under it. The ring keeps its velocity, smears into an ellipse along its direction of travel and wobbles round when the pointer stops; over a magnetic button it wraps the button's own outline and pulls it gently toward the pointer, over a card it blooms into a filled "View" disc, and over a paragraph it narrows to a caret that lands between real letters.
applications: magnetic calls to action in a hero
editorial long-reads with a text caret
accessibility: The native cursor is never hidden. The follower is two aria-hidden, pointer-events: none layers, so clicks, hover states and text selection reach the page untouched.

Fine pointers only, (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine): coarse devices render nothing, and a touch or pen event on a hybrid laptop hides the follower until the mouse moves again. The showcase works fully without it.
Any non-modifier key hides the follower so it never sits over a focus ring; focus styles are left alone, and moving the mouse brings it back.
"View" and "Drag" repeat what the content already says: each card is a named button, and the archive is a labelled, focusable region that scrolls with the arrow keys, by touch and by mouse drag.

A magnet moves toward the pointer, never away, with its travel capped so the hit area stays under the cursor; it uses the CSS translate property, so the element's own transform, press state and focus ring keep working.
effects.reducedMotion: The follower is decoration, so it is not rendered at all and magnets stay put. The native cursor, hover and focus states and the draggable archive work as usual; the archive stops where you let go, with no momentum or rubber band.
performance: One useRafLoop runs only while something moves and goes back to sleep once every spring is at rest; it also pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs.

Target rects, the scope rect and the layer origin are cached when a target is entered and refreshed at the start of the next frame after scroll or resize; every frame reads before it writes, and nothing is measured after a write.

Position, squash and stretch, press and presence are transforms and opacity. The outline morph writes the geometry of one SVG rect, only while a morph is moving, and identical values are never re-written.
Listeners are passive and installed only on fine-pointer devices with motion allowed; unmount removes them and clears every translate written to a magnet.

effects.name: Dot Grid Pointer Field
effects.description: A canvas grid of dots that leans away from the pointer, swells and warms to the accent colour, then springs back; a click sends a ripple ring through the field. The loop runs only while something is moving and stops the moment every spring has settled.
applications: section divider with a tactile response
accessibility: Keyboard path for every pointer action: focus the field (role="application", labelled and described), arrow keys move the influence point (Shift for bigger steps), Enter or Space sends a ripple, Esc clears it.
A visible "Send ripple" button offers the same burst without aiming, and the instruction line is always on screen.
Touch: vertical swipes keep scrolling the page (touch-action: pan-y); taps send ripples.
Purely decorative output — the canvas itself is aria-hidden and nothing is conveyed by colour alone.
effects.reducedMotion: The grid is drawn once as a static pattern; pointer, keyboard and ripple input do nothing and the field is no longer focusable (it becomes a labelled image).
performance: The rAF loop (useRafLoop) runs only while springs or ripples are moving: it stops at rest, pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, and restarts on the next pointer or key event.
Canvas backing store follows the box via ResizeObserver with devicePixelRatio capped at 2.
Dots are batched into five tint buckets: at most five fill() calls per frame, no per-dot style changes.
Springs use the shared `release` token, integrated in fixed 1/120 s substeps (frame-rate independent).

effects.name: Drag Reorder List
effects.description: A running order you rearrange by its drag handles: the picked-up row lifts on a token spring, its neighbours make room with layout animation (Motion Reorder) and every start time is recalculated. The handle is also a full keyboard control (Space to pick up, arrows to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel) with live announcements.
accessibility: Each row has a real handle button (44 px) named "Move <segment>, position n of N" and described by the keyboard instructions; aria-pressed shows when it is picked up.
Space or Enter picks up and drops, Up/Down move one place, Home/End jump to the ends, Escape restores the original order and leaving the handle drops the row.
An assertive live region announces pick-up, every move (with the new start time), drops, cancels and the result of pointer drags.
Focus stays on the moving handle throughout; the list is an ordered list, so position is also conveyed by the list semantics.
effects.reducedMotion: Rows swap places instantly and the picked-up row is marked by its border and shadow instead of scaling; a pointer drag still follows the pointer because that movement is user-controlled.
performance: Motion Reorder moves rows with transforms (layout projection); only the dragged row follows the pointer and nothing animates layout properties.
Start times are derived from the order in one pass per change; no timers or observers.
Per-row drag controls start the gesture from the handle only, so text selection and scrolling elsewhere stay native.

effects.name: Expanding Card Detail
effects.description: A programme of poster cards where the chosen card grows into a detail panel: card surface, poster and headline are shared elements (Motion layoutId) that travel on a token spring, the details fade in behind them, and focus moves into the panel while the grid goes inert.
applications: product cards opening a quick view
accessibility: Each card title is a real button (stretched over the card) with aria-haspopup="dialog", so the whole card is clickable but only one tab stop.
The panel is role="dialog" labelled by its heading; focus moves to its Close button, and Escape or Close return focus to the card that opened it.
While the panel is open the grid is inert (out of the tab order and the accessibility tree); an exiting panel is inert too, so Tab never lands in a closing view.
Posters are decorative SVG (aria-hidden); the event type, date and place are always real text, and a press outside the panel closes it like Escape does.
effects.reducedMotion: No shared-element travel: the panel and scrim fade in and out over 160 ms and the cards stay where they are.
performance: Motion animates the shared elements with transforms (FLIP-style projection); nothing animates width, height or top/left.

The poster artwork is a square emblem with its own layoutId, so it scales uniformly while the colour field around it morphs from card to panel shape; titles move by position only, so text never stretches.
Only the opened card and its panel are animated; the panel unmounts after its exit animation.

effects.name: Exploded View
effects.description: A procedural seven-part compact camera that comes apart along each part's own direction as a range slider goes from 0 to 1, with staggered ease-in-out so parts leave one after another. Part rows and 3D parts highlight each other, and the camera steps back to keep the whole assembly framed.
accessibility: Separation is a native range input (arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End) with a visible percentage; Assemble and Explode buttons jump to the ends.

Every part is a row button with its name and material in text: hovering or focusing a row lights the part, pointing at a part in the model marks its row, and clicking pins the highlight (aria-pressed).
The emissive highlight is never the only signal — the row gains an accent bar and the part name appears in the label over the view.
Without WebGL a flat exploded diagram is shown; the slider and the row highlights still drive it.
effects.reducedMotion: Parts follow the slider directly with no easing tail, and Assemble / Explode cut straight to the end state instead of gliding; the row accent bar no longer animates.
performance: frameloop="demand": a frame is rendered only while the separation is settling or a highlight changes; at rest nothing renders.
About 15 draw calls of primitive geometry, no textures except one baked floor blob; highlight is an emissive change on per-part materials (no extra passes).
Raycasting for hover happens only on pointer events (R3F), never per frame.
All geometries, materials and the canvas texture are created once and disposed on unmount.

effects.name: Flip Card 3D
effects.description: A two-sided card that turns over on a real button, never on hover alone. Both sides share one grid cell so the card is always as tall as its taller side, and a moving highlight plus a breathing shadow sell the rotation.
applications: product card with specifications on the back
accessibility: Flipping is a button press (Enter/Space), and each side has its own clearly named button; nothing is revealed by hover only.
The hidden side is inert, so its text and controls are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree; focus moves to the button on the side that just turned up.
Both sides are real DOM text in a shared grid cell, so the card grows with zoom and translation instead of clipping.
Sample pricing is labelled as sample data.
effects.reducedMotion: No rotation, lift or highlight sweep: the two sides cross-fade in 160 ms.
performance: Rotation is a single CSS transform transition; lift, highlight and shadow are three short WAAPI animations on transform/opacity that are cancelled on unmount.
backface-visibility hides the far side, so only one side is painted at a time.
No layout work during the flip: height is resolved once by CSS grid.

effects.name: FLIP Grid Reorder
effects.description: A filterable, sortable swatch library: tiles glide to their new cells with first-last-invert-play on the Web Animations API (the Motion Lab flip()), entering tiles scale in, leaving tiles fade out where they stood, and a new filter can interrupt a transition mid-flight without a jump.
accessibility: Filters and sort orders are native buttons with aria-pressed inside labelled groups; every change is a click or Enter/Space away.
A polite status line announces how many of the twelve materials are shown, which filter is on and how they are sorted.
Tiles are a plain list with real text names; leaving tiles are aria-hidden while they fade out, so the list never reads stale items.
Category and tone are written as text on every tile, never implied by colour or position alone.
effects.reducedMotion: Tiles jump straight to their new cells with no glide; leaving tiles are removed at once and entering tiles fade in over 160 ms.
performance: One measure pass before and one after a synchronous React commit (flushSync); everything that moves is a composited transform or opacity animation.
An interrupting change measures tiles where they visually are (mid-animation), cancels their animations and glides on from there.
Swatches are pure CSS gradients: no images, canvases or filters. Every animation is cancelled on unmount.

effects.name: Fullscreen Menu Curtain
effects.description: The menu button morphs into a close icon while a clip-path curtain opens from the button, the top edge or the side, revealing oversized navigation links that rise out of masks in sequence. Everything is contained in its own stage and reverses cleanly when interrupted.
accessibility: A real button with aria-expanded/aria-controls and a text label that switches between "Menu" and "Close".
Opening moves focus to the first link; Tab cycles between the links and the close button; Escape closes and returns focus to the button.
The closed navigation and, while open, the page behind it are inert, so hidden content cannot be focused or read.
The current page is marked with aria-current and a text marker, not colour alone.
effects.reducedMotion: No clip-path reveal or rising links: the menu appears and disappears with a 160 ms opacity fade and the icon swaps without rotating.
performance: Pure CSS transitions on clip-path, transform and opacity; state lives in one data attribute, so the reveal is interruptible mid-flight for free.
No JavaScript runs per frame and nothing is measured.
The curtain is positioned inside the component (not the viewport), so it never triggers page-level layout.

effects.name: Grain Gradient Mesh
effects.description: Three or four soft colour fields — paper, ink and one accent from the theme — drift very slowly on compositor transforms under a film-grain tile that is generated once with canvas2d. No per-frame canvas work and no blur filters.
accessibility: The gradient and grain layers are aria-hidden decoration; copy sits on a solid surface card, so text contrast never depends on where a field drifts.
Drift is slow (47–89 s periods at 1×), low-contrast and never flashes.
Colours come from theme tokens (paper = --mk-bg, ink = --mk-ink, one accent), so light, dark and always-dark stages all stay coherent.
effects.reducedMotion: No drift: the fields render as a still composition. The animation is gated twice — by useStudioMotion() and by a prefers-reduced-motion media query.
performance: Each field is a single radial-gradient element animated with transform only; no filter, no per-frame JavaScript.
The grain is one 128 px PNG data URL generated once per page and cached; it tiles via background-image.
Animations are paused (animation-play-state) while the element is offscreen.

effects.name: Horizontal Scroll Gallery
effects.description: Vertical scrolling drives a pinned, horizontal track of plates on a scrubbed GSAP timeline with smoothing and per-card snap. Tabbing through cards scrolls the container to the matching position, so keyboard focus is never off-screen.
accessibility: Cards are toggle buttons in a list; focusing a card that is off-screen scrolls the container to the position where that card is visible (the pinned frame uses overflow: clip, so the browser cannot scroll it sideways behind the timeline).
The scroll container is a focusable, labelled region: arrow keys, Space and Page keys drive the horizontal travel.
A text counter ("03 / 06") reports position; pinned state of a card is exposed with aria-pressed and a text mark, not colour alone.
effects.reducedMotion: No pinning or scrub. The track becomes a native horizontal overflow list with scroll-snap, scrolled directly by touch, trackpad, or keyboard focus.
performance: Pinning is CSS position: sticky; ScrollTrigger scrubs a single timeline that moves one transform on the track.
Track length and snap points are measured once per layout; a ResizeObserver rebuilds the timeline when the container width changes.
useGSAP with revertOnUpdate reverts tweens, inline styles and the ScrollTrigger on unmount and on every param change.

effects.name: Hotspot Annotations
effects.description: Four annotations anchored to a procedural field radio. Markers are projected on rendered frames only, fade and turn inert when the object hides them, and choosing one — from the marker or the always-readable list — glides the camera to frame it and opens its description. Esc returns to the full view.
accessibility: The same four annotations are a real ordered list of disclosure buttons (aria-expanded / aria-controls) outside the canvas — the stable keyboard and screen-reader path; keyboard focus frames an item, Enter toggles it, Esc resets.
Floating markers are pointer shortcuts only (tabindex=-1, aria-hidden), so nothing is announced twice; a polite live region confirms which feature is framed.
Markers hidden behind the radio fade and become inert, so a faded, low-contrast marker can never be clicked or focused; the list always works.
The canvas itself is focusable via the kit's OrbitInspect (arrows orbit, + / − zoom, 0 resets) and carries an accessible name; wheel zoom only applies while it has focus.
Without WebGL a front-view SVG with the same numbering is shown and the list still opens every description.
effects.reducedMotion: Camera moves become cuts (CameraRig with reduced motion), orbit damping is off and the marker fade transition is removed.
performance: frameloop="demand": frames render only during a camera glide or an orbit; marker projection and the four occlusion rays run inside those frames, so an idle scene costs nothing.
About 16 draw calls: one rounded-box case, shared box geometry for panels, instanced feet and strap posts; perforations and the tuning scale are canvas textures drawn once.
Generated environment lighting (LightingRig studio-soft, PMREM sized by quality); no shadow pass — a baked contact blob grounds the object.
Every geometry, material and canvas texture created imperatively is disposed on unmount.

effects.name: Image Ripple Distortion
effects.description: A poster series drawn on the fly with canvas2d in the theme's own colours and type, swapped by a GLSL ripple: a displacement front with chromatic split travels out from where you click and reveals the next poster. Hovering stirs a faint ripple under the pointer.
accessibility: A real "Next poster" button is the keyboard path; clicking the poster is only a pointer shortcut that also chooses the ripple origin.
Poster title and subtitle are DOM text in a polite live region, and the canvas label names the current poster, so nothing lives only in pixels.
Distortion is brief, low-frequency and user-triggered; there is no autoplay and no flashing.
Without WebGL the same generated posters are shown as images that cross-fade.
effects.reducedMotion: No displacement, chromatic split or hover ripple: Next cross-fades the posters in 160 ms.
performance: frameloop="demand": frames render only during a transition or while the hover ripple is fading; at rest nothing renders.
One full-frame quad, one draw call; three poster CanvasTextures sized by the quality profile (no mipmaps), regenerated only when the theme or fonts change and disposed every time.
Fonts are awaited with document.fonts.load before the posters are redrawn, so textures never bake a fallback face.

effects.name: Kinetic Marquee
effects.description: A two-rail infinite marquee that borrows momentum from page scroll and pointer travel: velocity adds speed, leans the type into a skew and can briefly reverse the rail. It eases to a stop on hover or focus and has a visible pause control.

params.label: Phrases (separate with /)
params.default: Design intelligence / Motion engineering / Digital experiences

accessibility: A visible Pause/Play button (aria-pressed) stops all movement, satisfying WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.
The phrases are exposed once as a list; every repeated copy and the secondary rail are aria-hidden.
Hovering the band or moving focus into it eases the rails to a stop so the text can be read.
effects.reducedMotion: No loop runs: both rails are static, skew is removed and the pause control is replaced by a "motion off" note.
performance: One rAF loop (useRafLoop, paused offscreen) writes one transform per rail; nothing is laid out per frame.
Scroll and pointer listeners are passive and only accumulate a delta that the loop consumes.
Copies are created from a ResizeObserver measurement: just enough to cover the container plus one.

effects.name: Layered Depth Stack
effects.description: An exploded-interface illustration: four CSS-drawn UI layers pulled apart along Z under a perspective camera. A range input sets the separation, a second one (or the pointer) turns the view. Pure CSS 3D, no canvas.
applications: feature hero showing how a screen is built
accessibility: Separation and view angle are native range inputs with visible labels and value text, so everything the pointer does is available from the keyboard.
The illustration is one labelled image (role="img"); the layer names and what each layer holds are listed as ordinary text beside it.
Pointer tilt is an enhancement on top of the sliders and never the only way to see a layer.
effects.reducedMotion: Pointer-driven tilt is switched off and the layers move without easing; the sliders still work because the movement is then directly user-controlled.
performance: Only custom properties change: the browser recomputes five transforms, with no layout and no JavaScript animation loop.
Pointer updates are coalesced to one style write per animation frame.
Layers are plain elements with borders and gradients; there are no images, filters or canvases.

effects.name: Like Heart Morph
effects.description: Like and save controls that morph instead of swapping icons: the heart fills from its centre on an overshoot spring with a ring and ray burst, the bookmark ribbon unrolls downward. Undoing plays a shorter, quieter reverse and rapid toggling never desynchronises.
accessibility: Both controls are toggle buttons with aria-pressed: the constant visible caption ("Like 128", "Save") is the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3), state is conveyed by aria-pressed and the filled icon, and the like count is real text.
State is carried by fill and caption, not colour alone; the burst is aria-hidden decoration.
Works with Enter/Space; focus ring is visible on the whole control; targets are at least 44 px.
effects.reducedMotion: The icon fill cross-fades in 160 ms; no spring, ring or rays.
performance: Transform and opacity only, on a handful of SVG nodes.
Each toggle cancels the previous sequence and starts from the current computed transform, so interruptions are seamless and nothing accumulates.
Sequences are cancelled on unmount.

effects.name: Line Chart Morph
effects.description: A line and area chart that morphs between time ranges by interpolating data values, not pixels: the y-axis rescales continuously, gridlines cross-fade and the line never tears. A crosshair reads every point by pointer or arrow keys.
applications: analytics overview with a range switcher
accessibility: The range switcher is a native radio group (arrow keys move between ranges).
The plot is a focusable slider: ←/→ step through points, Home/End jump, and aria-valuetext announces label and value.
A visually-hidden data table mirrors the visible series; the SVG itself is aria-hidden.
Single series: nothing is encoded by colour alone, and all figures use tabular numerals.
effects.reducedMotion: Switching ranges swaps the dataset and axis instantly; crosshair and tooltip still work.
performance: Both datasets are resampled once to a shared resolution, so each frame is one array lerp and two path strings.
The rAF loop only runs during a morph and is cancelled on unmount or interruption.
Re-measures with ResizeObserver; no layout reads inside the animation loop.

effects.name: Liquid Glass Lens
effects.description: A thick glass lens you drag and throw across an editorial page drawn in the theme's own colours and type. A GLSL pass refracts the page through a flat-topped, round-edged SDF lens (pill, circle or squircle): the centre stays sharp while the rim bends the page, splits it into spectral colour and catches one light that follows your pointer, and the glass casts a soft shadow away from that light.
applications: hero over a headline or key visual
product detail loupe over packaging or a label
image inspection: drag a magnifier-style glass across a chart, map or scan
glass control surface (tab bar, toolbar) prototype over live content
accessibility: The lens is a focusable control named "Glass lens" with visible focus: arrow keys move it, Shift with an arrow moves it four times further, Home centres it; its new position is announced in a polite live region.
Shape is chosen with real buttons (aria-pressed) and a Centre button repeats the Home key, so nothing depends on dragging.
The page under the glass is decorative sample content; the canvas carries a name and a description of what it shows.
Without WebGL the same page is drawn as SVG under a CSS glass panel that is dragged and keyed the same way.
effects.reducedMotion: The lens follows the pointer or keys directly: no momentum, rubber band, stretch or lift animation, shape changes snap, and the light stays at its resting angle. Everything stays operable.
performance: frameloop="demand": frames render only while the lens is held, gliding or settling, or while the light eases after the pointer; at rest nothing renders.
One full-frame quad and one draw call. Pixels away from the lens and its shadow take a single texture read; the lens itself takes 6, 9 or 12 spectral taps by quality level.

The page texture is drawn once at the drawing-buffer size (CSS size × the profile's DPR cap), with mipmaps for frost; it is redrawn only on theme, font or resize changes (debounced) and disposed each time.
The lens physics runs in the R3F frame loop (or a rAF loop that pauses offscreen in the fallback) and stops when everything has settled.

effects.name: Lottie Micro-interactions
effects.description: Six hand-animated icons authored as original Lottie data in typed code: menu crosses to close on a spring, play splits into pause, an ink drop falls into the bookmark, the bell rings with a lagging clapper, the heart bursts, the sun folds into a moon. Hover previews each wind-up, a click commits from that exact frame and can reverse at any frame, and colours come from theme tokens through CSS.
applications: app bar menu and theme toggles
like and save actions in a feed
replacing static icon sets with animated ones that share one data format with After Effects exports
accessibility: Every icon is a real button with a constant accessible name: toggles expose aria-pressed (Play, Like, Save, New-episode alerts, Night mode); the queue button is a disclosure with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and its panel leaves the accessibility tree when closed.

State never relies on colour or motion alone: the shapes differ (lines vs cross, outline vs filled, slashed vs ringing bell, sun vs moon), the like count and "Playing / Paused" are real text, and the animated drawing is aria-hidden.
Keyboard: Enter and Space toggle; focus-visible previews the same wind-up as hover; each timeline lane is a labelled native slider (arrow keys step one frame, leaving the lane plays the icon home).
Targets are at least 44 px; focus rings use --mk-focus; colours map to tokens, and forced-colors mode redraws the icons in system colours.
effects.reducedMotion: Hover and focus previews are off and nothing travels: a state change jumps the Lottie to the final frame of its segment (goToAndStop) under a 160 ms cross-fade, the queue opens without sliding and the cover swaps sun for moon with a fade. Scrubbing still works because it is direct manipulation.
performance: lottie-web’s light SVG player is imported lazily, once, and shared; each icon owns one instance that is destroyed on unmount (StrictMode-safe).

lottie-web only ticks while an instance plays, so an idle toolbar runs no animation frame; the timeline playheads are written straight to the DOM from enterFrame events, with no React render per frame.
Until the player has painted, and wherever it cannot run, each icon shows a static SVG of its rest frame rendered from the same data, so the swap is invisible and nothing is lost if lottie fails.

Colours are CSS on the rendered SVG, so theme or palette changes restyle every icon with no data rebuild; only the stroke-weight param rebuilds the data, and each icon keeps its frame across the rebuild.

effects.name: Magnetic Button
effects.description: Call-to-action buttons that lean toward a nearby pointer and spring home when it leaves. The pull fades smoothly to zero at the edge of the field, the label floats a little further than the body for depth, and the physics is a hand-rolled token spring on one paused-when-idle rAF loop.
accessibility: Real <button> elements: Enter and Space activate them and the result is announced through a polite status line.
Keyboard focus gets the same engaged state as hover (arrow turns, surface shifts, field lights up when shown) plus a 2 px focus ring that travels with the button.
Magnetism is decoration only: it never moves a button away from the pointer, and the hit area always stays under the cursor.
Both buttons are at least 56 px; the icon-only button has an accessible name.
effects.reducedMotion: No magnetism and no press squash: buttons stay put, and hover/focus only change colour and turn the arrow without animating.
performance: One useRafLoop drives every magnet; it starts on pointer movement inside the stage and stops itself once all springs are at rest, so an idle page runs no frames.
Each frame reads the static anchor rects first, then writes transforms (no layout thrash; the moving element is never measured).
Springs use the motion tokens with sub-stepped semi-implicit Euler integration, stable at any frame rate.
Disabled entirely for coarse pointers (hover: none / pointer: coarse) and under reduced motion: no listeners do work.

effects.name: Morph Submit Button
effects.description: A submit button that tells the whole story of a request: the pill collapses into a circle whose progress arc fills ever more slowly while waiting, then either completes and draws a check or shakes twice with an exclamation mark before reopening as "Try again". Every step starts from the current on-screen state, so resets and re-submits never jump.
accessibility: A real form with a labelled email field; the submit button keeps focus through every state and is aria-busy while the request runs.
Busy and finished states use aria-disabled (not disabled), so focus is never dropped; the button name always matches its state ("Sending…", "On the list", "Try again").
One polite live region announces sending, success and failure in words, with an icon as a second cue; colour is never the only signal.
Validation marks the field aria-invalid and points to the message with aria-describedby; Reset demo works from the keyboard at any moment.
effects.reducedMotion: The button keeps its pill shape: labels and colours change in place (no morph, arc, check drawing or shake) and the status text carries progress.
performance: The width morph runs on one button inside a fixed-width slot, so only that box is laid out per frame; ring, check and shake are stroke/transform/opacity animations.
Each phase reads the current computed width, opacity or dash offset before animating, so interrupted runs continue from where they are instead of restarting.
All animations and timers are tracked in one set and cancelled on reset, on resubmission and on unmount.

effects.name: Morphing Nav Pill
effects.description: A tab bar whose active indicator is one shared element: it glides between tabs and stretches to each label width on a token spring (Motion layoutId), while a faint ghost previews the hovered or focused tab and the panels cross-fade in a fixed-height stack.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel", aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby are wired with useId.
Roving tabindex: Arrow Left/Right wrap, Home/End jump; activation follows focus or waits for Enter/Space depending on the activation param.
The indicator and ghost are decorative (aria-hidden); the selected tab is also marked by aria-selected and label weight/colour, not by position alone.
Hidden panels are inert, so their content is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
effects.reducedMotion: The indicator jumps to the selected tab with no layout animation, the ghost is removed and panels swap with a 160 ms opacity fade.
performance: Motion animates the shared indicator with transforms (FLIP); tabs themselves never resize.
All panels share one grid cell, so the card height is the tallest panel and switching causes no layout shift.
Only two small elements are ever animated; no listeners outside the component.

effects.name: Number Ticker
effects.description: An odometer-style numeric transition: each digit is its own rolling column that travels through the intermediate digits in the direction of change, with locale-aware formatting and a delta chip that states the change in words.
applications: live counter in a dashboard header
accessibility: The value is exposed once, as a single formatted text node in a polite status region; the rolling digit columns are aria-hidden.
The delta chip pairs its arrow with a signed number and the words up/down, so direction never depends on colour.
Tabular numerals and fixed-width digit cells keep the layout from shifting while digits roll.
effects.reducedMotion: Digits swap instantly with no roll; entering characters do not slide.
performance: Only changed digits animate, each as one transform-only WAAPI animation on a short strip (≤ 10 cells).
Strips collapse back to a single cell when the roll finishes; animations are cancelled on unmount or retarget.

effects.name: Orbit Inspect Controls
effects.description: Accessible orbit inspection of a procedural architectural maquette: drag to orbit with damping and limits, zoom only when the viewer is focused (or with a pinch), and a full keyboard and button path. Shadows are baked once for the fixed key light, so the scene renders only while the camera moves.
accessibility: The viewer wrapper is focusable (role="application", labelled, described by the visible instruction line, aria-keyshortcuts): arrows orbit, + / − zoom, 0 or Home resets.
Every pointer gesture has a button: rotate left/right, tilt up/down, zoom in/out and reset, all ≥ 44 px with visible focus.
No scroll hijack: the wheel zooms only while the viewer has focus; ctrl/⌘ + wheel (trackpad pinch) zooms while hovering; touch uses touch-action: pan-y so vertical swipes still scroll the page.
After each move settles, a polite live region reports the view (angle, elevation, zoom); the on-canvas readout is aria-hidden to avoid per-frame chatter.
Without WebGL an SVG axonometric drawn from the same model data is shown and the camera buttons are disabled with an explanation.
effects.reducedMotion: Damping and the idle turntable are switched off, so every orbit, zoom and reset is a direct cut with no easing tail; dragging still follows the pointer 1:1.
performance: frameloop="demand": nothing renders at rest; frames are requested only while the camera moves (including the damping tail) or the optional turntable runs.

About 15 draw calls: shared box geometry, instanced columns, steps, trees and figures; no shadow-map pass at any quality level — ground shadows are baked once into a canvas texture for the fixed key light.
Generated environment lighting (PMREM, sized by the quality profile) instead of a downloaded HDRI; NeutralToneMapping keeps paper white and the accent hue true.
All imperatively created geometries, materials and canvas textures are disposed on unmount.

effects.name: Parallax Depth Layers
effects.description: A paper-cut landscape whose layers travel at depth-scaled rates as it passes through the scroll container. One scroll-progress custom property drives every layer in CSS — no animation library, no per-layer JavaScript.
accessibility: The scene is a figure with a text caption; every moving layer is aria-hidden decoration.
The scroll container is a focusable, labelled region so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.
Motion is strictly scroll-linked: nothing moves unless the reader scrolls, and layer travel is capped by the Strength param.
effects.reducedMotion: The scroll listener is not attached and the progress property stays at 0, so the scene renders as a static, centred composition.
performance: One passive, rAF-batched scroll listener (useScrollProgress) writes a single custom property; the browser resolves each layer transform in CSS.
Layers animate transform only and are promoted with will-change; no layout or paint work per frame beyond compositing.
Layers are oversized inside an overflow: clip frame, so travel never reveals an edge and never changes layout.

effects.name: Particle Field GPU
effects.description: THREE.Points with a custom ShaderMaterial: every particle's position is a pure function of its seed and time, integrated along the curl of a stream function in the vertex shader, so the field braids and drifts with zero CPU work per particle. The pointer pushes particles aside or draws them in.
accessibility: A visible Pause / Play button (aria-pressed) stops the continuous motion at any time (WCAG 2.2.2).
Keyboard path for the pointer influence: focus the field (role="application", labelled and described), arrows move the influence point, Shift for bigger steps, Esc releases it.
Works on light and dark stages: ink particles with ordinary alpha on light surfaces, additive light on dark ones; colours come from the theme tokens.
Decorative: the canvas has a label and a text description; without WebGL an SVG of the same flow field's streamlines is shown.
effects.reducedMotion: A single static frame of the field is rendered (frameloop="demand", time frozen); the pointer has no effect and the field is not focusable.
performance: One draw call (THREE.Points); per frame only uniforms change — positions come from per-particle seeds in the vertex shader (7 Euler steps of an analytic curl field).
Particle count is the param × the quality profile's density (12 000 → 7 200 on medium, 3 600 on low); the canvas pauses offscreen via StudioCanvas.
frameloop="always" only while playing; paused or reduced motion switches to "demand" and renders only on pointer input.
Geometry and material are created imperatively and disposed on unmount or when the count changes.

effects.name: Poll Result Bars
effects.description: A single-choice poll whose option rows turn into result bars in place: fills slide out to each share on a staggered WAAPI timeline while the percentages count up in lockstep with each bar’s own eased progress. Your pick keeps its spot, gains a check and "Your vote", and you can change it.
accessibility: Native radio group inside a fieldset with the question as its legend: arrow keys move the choice, Enter or the Vote button submits.
Results are a list whose rows read as "option, percent", plus "Your vote" and "Leading" as words with an icon; the accent fill is never the only cue.
A polite live region reads the final results once; the counting numbers are not announced frame by frame.
Focus moves to "Change vote" after voting and back to the checked radio after choosing to change it.
effects.reducedMotion: Bars appear at their final width with a 160 ms opacity fade and the percentages are shown immediately.
performance: Each fill is a full-width layer translated inside a clipped track (transform only), so rounded ends never distort.
Counting reads getComputedTiming().progress of each bar inside one useRafLoop that runs only while bars move.
The final transform is the inline style, so no fill-mode animations linger; everything is cancelled on unmount.

effects.name: Press Depth Button
effects.description: Keycap buttons with real layered depth: the face sits on a visible side band over a soft contact shadow. Pressing drives the face down along Z while the shadow collapses; letting go springs it back on a CSS linear() curve sampled from a motion-token spring. Busy keys stay half-pressed, disabled keys sink flush and rise when they unlock.
applications: primary action on a device-like control panel
accessibility: Native buttons: Space presses on keydown and activates on keyup, Enter activates once (auto-repeat is ignored); the pressed look follows the key, the pointer and blur alike.
Busy and locked keys use aria-disabled instead of disabled, so they stay focusable; the locked key explains itself through aria-describedby.
The panel display is a polite live region that announces printing and completion; the print counter is plain text.
Focus ring wraps the whole key including its depth band; every key is at least 56 px tall.
Label text keeps 4.5:1 or better against every key face in both themes.
effects.reducedMotion: Press, release and unlock happen instantly with no spring or shadow animation, and the progress bar is replaced by the display text.
performance: Press and release are CSS transform/opacity transitions; the spring is precomputed once with springToLinear(), so no JavaScript runs per frame.
The progress bar is a single scaleX transition; label swaps share one grid cell, so busy states never change the key width.
Timers are cleared on unmount and on every new print.

effects.name: Progress Orbit Loader
effects.description: One SVG loader for the whole life of a job: while the size is unknown a dash orbits on eased turns and breathes in length, then it hands over to a determinate arc with a satellite marking the leading edge and a tabular-figure percentage that never jitters, and finally settles on "Done".
applications: inline busy indicator in buttons and rows
accessibility: role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max; aria-valuenow and a spoken aria-valuetext only while the amount is known (indeterminate omits aria-valuenow, as ARIA specifies).
A separate polite live region announces phase changes (preparing, exporting, complete) instead of every percent.
The readout uses tabular figures, so the number never shifts width; the ring and satellite are aria-hidden decoration.
Restart is a real button reachable by keyboard.
effects.reducedMotion: No orbit, breathing or easing: a static quarter ring with "Preparing" while indeterminate, then the ring and percentage update in place without transitions.
performance: Indeterminate motion is two CSS keyframe animations (rotation on a group, dash length on one circle); they unmount the moment the job becomes determinate.
Determinate progress changes one stroke-dashoffset and one rotation per update (a few per second), smoothed by CSS transitions.
The simulated job is one timer chain, cleared on restart and unmount.

effects.name: Pull-to-Reveal Sheet
effects.description: A transit-stop bottom sheet over a drawn map: pull its header between peek, half and full snap points, push past the ends to feel it rubber-band, and fling it to skip a stop. Release velocity picks the snap, a token spring carries that velocity, and the map dims in proportion to how far the sheet is open.
accessibility: The sheet header is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls: Enter/Space toggles peek ↔ open, Up/Down step between snap points, Home/End jump to full or peek.
Visible Expand and Collapse step buttons do everything a drag does with a single press (WCAG 2.5.7); they stay focusable at the limits (aria-disabled) so focus is never dropped.

Escape collapses the sheet from anywhere inside it and returns focus to the header; at peek the hidden content is inert, and when open the list scrolls within the visible part, so nothing focusable is ever off-screen.
A polite status line reports the sheet position after drags, presses and keys; the map is decorative (aria-hidden) and every departure is written as text.
effects.reducedMotion: No spring travel: snap points, buttons and keys jump straight to the target and the scrim follows instantly. Dragging still tracks the pointer because that movement is under the user’s control.
performance: The sheet moves by one motion value (translateY); the scrim opacity is derived from it, so dragging causes no React renders.
Snap offsets are recomputed only when the frame is resized (ResizeObserver), and the list height changes only when a snap settles.
The map is a single static SVG; no layout properties are animated.

effects.name: Reaction Burst
effects.description: Reaction toggles that throw a short burst of matching shapes on a ballistic arc — launch cone, gravity, air drag and spin — while the count pops. Particles are drawn from a fixed pool on one canvas that sleeps when nothing is in the air.
accessibility: Each reaction is a real toggle button (aria-pressed) whose name includes its label and text count.
A polite status line confirms the change in words; the canvas is decorative and aria-hidden.
Pressed state is shown by a filled icon and an inverted chip, not by colour alone; targets are 44 px tall.
effects.reducedMotion: No particles: the count updates and the chip gives one brief opacity pulse.
performance: Fixed pool of 160 particles, reused; a burst never allocates.
One canvas, DPR capped at 2, driven by useRafLoop and switched off as soon as the last particle dies.
Shapes are cached Path2D objects; no layout reads inside the loop.

effects.name: Rive State Machine
effects.description: Two Rive state machines driven only by DOM controls. Birb idles on a lit stage, looks up when the pointer (or a tap) comes in above its head and dances on a real toggle button; a native five-star radio group previews on hover, focus or drag and commits into a second machine. A reusable RiveCanvas loads the runtime lazily from your own origin, sizes itself to its element and stops drawing offscreen.
applications: mascot or onboarding character that reacts to the user
animated rating, feedback or survey control
empty, success and error states with a character
interactive product illustration in a hero
accessibility: The canvases are aria-hidden; meaning lives in the DOM: the stage is a labelled image whose name follows the state machine (idle, looking up, dancing) and every input has a native control.

Dance is a toggle button with aria-pressed, Look up is a plain button, so keyboard users get every reaction the pointer gets; a polite status line announces the look-up and pause changes the canvas cannot speak.

The rating is a native fieldset of five radio buttons laid over the drawn stars: arrow keys move and commit, hover and focus preview, the committed value is announced politely, and a double focus ring stays visible on the gradient.
The idle loop runs longer than five seconds, so the stage has a visible Pause/Play button (WCAG 2.2.2).
If the runtime or a file cannot load, the controls keep working: the rating falls back to drawn DOM stars and the stage says what is missing.
The breakdown under the stars is labelled sample data; every bar also has its count as text, and the visitor’s own row is marked by weight as well as colour.
effects.reducedMotion: Nothing plays on its own: Birb holds a still idle frame and pointer reactions are off. Dance, Look up and Play are explicit controls, so they still animate and Birb settles back to a still frame afterwards. Rating changes jump straight to the final frame of each state (state machine stopped, the matching animation scrubbed to its end) with a 160 ms cross-fade.
performance: The Rive runtime is a dynamic import inside an effect, so other pages never download it. Its JavaScript (about 129 KB gzipped as published, less once minified) and WASM (about 374 KB gzipped) load once per page, from your own origin: the WASM and fallback URLs are props, and Rive’s asset CDN is off.
Each canvas sizes its drawing buffer from a ResizeObserver with the device pixel ratio capped at 2, and redraws on DPR changes.
Rendering stops while a canvas is offscreen or the tab is hidden, and the rating state machine settles: once its stars have landed no frames are drawn until the input changes.

The .riv bytes are fetched once and shared by every instance; each Rive instance is released with cleanup() on unmount, and loads that finish after unmount are dropped, so StrictMode double mounts and Replay leave nothing behind.

effects.name: Scramble Decode
effects.description: Text resolves from churning glyphs to the final string in a left-to-right sweep. Frames come from a seeded hash, so the same seed always produces the same animation, and every character sits in a fixed 1ch cell so nothing shifts.
accessibility: The real sentence is rendered once as visually hidden text; the animated cells are aria-hidden, so assistive tech never hears the scramble.
Replay is a real button; hovering the text or keyboard-focusing the button also replays, so no interaction is pointer-only.
Progress is not conveyed by colour alone: a resolved counter accompanies the progress rule.
effects.reducedMotion: The final string is shown immediately; replay only runs a 160 ms opacity fade and hover does nothing.
performance: Cells are updated through textContent/data attributes only when their glyph changes; React does not re-render per frame.
The rAF loop (useRafLoop) idles when no decode is running and pauses offscreen or in a hidden tab.
Fixed 1ch cells and nowrap words mean zero layout shift during the churn.

effects.name: Scroll Camera Dolly
effects.description: Scrolling a self-contained region moves a camera along a Catmull-Rom spline through a fogged colonnade of gateways towards a low sun, with look-ahead targeting and three captions tied to progress ranges. The canvas renders only when progress changes.
accessibility: The scroll area is a focusable, labelled region, so arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Space scroll it like any other overflow container.
Captions are real text that stays in the DOM; only their opacity follows progress, and a progress bar shows position.
With reduced motion the three captioned viewpoints become numbered step buttons instead of a scroll.
Without WebGL a drawn still of the colonnade is shown with all three captions as a list.
effects.reducedMotion: No scroll-driven travel: the region stops scrolling and three step buttons cut between fixed viewpoints, each with its caption (one rendered frame per step).
performance: frameloop="demand": scroll progress is read in a passive, rAF-batched listener and a frame is requested only when it changes; easing towards the new progress stops requesting frames once settled.
Columns and lintels are two instanced meshes, so the whole scene is five draw calls.
Caption opacity is written straight to style, with no React re-render per scroll frame.

effects.name: Scroll Pin Chapters
effects.description: A pinned panel whose chapters — numeral, title, line illustration — hand over to each other on a scrubbed GSAP timeline as the container scrolls. Progress dots are real buttons that scroll to each chapter.
accessibility: The scroll container is a focusable, labelled region, so arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Space scroll it without a pointer.
Every chapter stays in the DOM as a section with its own heading; only opacity/transform/clip-path are animated, so assistive tech can read all chapters in order.
Progress dots are buttons named "Go to chapter N: title"; the active one carries aria-current="step" and is also distinguished by shape, not colour alone.
Illustrations are decorative and aria-hidden; nothing is conveyed by motion alone.
effects.reducedMotion: No pinning and no scrub: chapters render as ordinary stacked sections in the scroll container, and the dots jump to a section without smooth scrolling.
performance: Pinning uses CSS position: sticky (compositor-driven, no jitter in nested scrollers); ScrollTrigger only scrubs one timeline.
One ScrollTrigger on the timeline, never on child tweens; transforms, opacity and clip-path only.
useGSAP scope + revertOnUpdate reverts tweens, inline styles and the trigger on unmount or param change; the ResizeObserver that refreshes the trigger is disconnected with it.
React state changes only when the active chapter index changes, not per scroll frame.

effects.name: Scroll Progress Rail
effects.description: A reading-progress rail whose segments fill as each section crosses the reading line and whose marker names the current section. Driven entirely by CSS scroll-driven animations (scroll() and named view() timelines), with a rAF-batched JavaScript fallback where animation-timeline is unsupported.
accessibility: The rail is a nav landmark; each marker is a button named after its section that scrolls it to the reading line and moves focus to the section heading.
The current marker carries aria-current="location" (set by an IntersectionObserver in both drivers, since CSS cannot set ARIA state).
Current and completed states differ by fill length and weight as well as colour; the percentage readout is decorative and aria-hidden.
The scroll container is a focusable, labelled region for keyboard scrolling.
effects.reducedMotion: The rail is scroll-linked feedback rather than autonomous motion, so it keeps tracking position; marker label transitions are removed and marker clicks jump instead of smooth-scrolling.
performance: CSS driver: scroll() and view() timelines run on the compositor with zero scroll listeners; timeline-scope lets markers outside the sections subscribe to them.
Fallback driver: one passive, rAF-batched listener (useScrollProgress) reads all section rects first, then writes custom properties — no interleaved layout.
Support: animation-timeline + timeline-scope in Chromium 116+ and Safari 26+; other engines get the fallback automatically via CSS.supports().

effects.name: Aurora Shader Plane
effects.description: A full-bleed GLSL background of slow, banded light built from domain-warped value noise. One draw call, one triangle pair, no textures.
accessibility: Purely decorative: the canvas has a label and nothing depends on it; keep text contrast by placing copy on a scrim or solid surface.
No flashing: luminance changes are slow and low-amplitude (well under three flashes per second).
effects.reducedMotion: Renders a single static frame (render-on-demand, time frozen); pointer influence is disabled.
performance: A single full-screen quad: fill-rate bound, so cost scales with canvas pixels — StudioCanvas clamps DPR per quality profile.
Loop pauses when offscreen or the tab is hidden; reduced motion switches to frameloop="demand".
Material and geometry are disposed by R3F on unmount; no render targets or textures are allocated.

effects.name: Skeleton Shimmer Handoff
effects.description: Skeleton rows that hand off to real content with a staggered cross-fade and zero layout shift. One shimmer layer, clipped to the union of every bone with a measured clip-path, sweeps the whole list with a single pseudo-element animation; skeleton and content share each row’s grid cell and line-height-locked geometry.
applications: feed or reading list first load
accessibility: The list region is aria-busy while loading, and a polite live region says "Loading reading list…" and then how many articles arrived.
Skeleton bones and the shimmer layer are aria-hidden; real content only enters the accessibility tree once it exists.
Reload is a real button that stays focusable while busy (aria-disabled), so keyboard focus is never lost.
Titles reserve two lines and metadata one, so zooming or narrow containers never push rows around when content lands.
effects.reducedMotion: Bones stay static (no sweep or pulse), and the handoff becomes a single 160 ms opacity cross-fade with no stagger or rise.
performance: Exactly one infinite animation while loading: a transform (sweep) or opacity (pulse) keyframe on one pseudo-element, removed as soon as content is ready.
The clip-path is rebuilt only on resize (ResizeObserver, rAF-batched), never per frame.
Handoff is one createSequence timeline (transform/opacity) that is cancelled on unmount and on every reload.

effects.name: Split Line Reveal
effects.description: Headline words rise from behind a clipping mask with a parent→child stagger, sequenced on the Web Animations API so it can be interrupted, replayed and cleaned up.
accessibility: The heading exposes the full sentence through aria-label; the split spans are aria-hidden so screen readers do not read word by word.
Text is real DOM text: selectable, translatable and zoomable.
effects.reducedMotion: Words are shown immediately with no transform; the sequence collapses to its end state.
performance: Animates transform and opacity only (compositor-friendly).
Splits by word, not by character, to keep the animated layer count low.
The sequence is cancelled on unmount so no animations outlive the component.

effects.name: Spotlight Border Card
effects.description: A grid of selectable module cards lit by a single moving spotlight: one pointer listener on the grid hands each card its local pointer position, and pure CSS paints a radial light into a 1px masked border ring (and, optionally, a faint glow on the surface), so neighbouring cards catch the edge of the same light. Keyboard focus lights the focused card on its own.
accessibility: Each card is a toggle: a real button (stretched over the card) with aria-pressed, described by the card text; a polite status line counts the selection.
Keyboard focus lights the focused card fully and draws a 2px focus outline, independent of the pointer.
Selection is shown with a text label ("Added") and a check, not by the light or colour alone; the light layers are decorative pseudo-elements.
effects.reducedMotion: The light no longer travels with the pointer: hovering a card shows a static lit border instead, and focus still lights the focused card.
performance: One pointermove listener on the grid, batched to one rAF: all card rects are read first, then each card gets two custom properties, so there is no layout thrash.
The light is two gradient pseudo-elements per card; the border ring is a mask (content-box exclude), so nothing is re-laid out.
Smooth follow uses registered @property lengths with a CSS transition rather than a JavaScript loop; touch pointers are ignored.

effects.name: Story Progress Segments
effects.description: A Stories-style viewer with segmented progress: each segment fills on a WAAPI timeline and advances the story, the left third goes back and the rest goes forward, pressing and holding pauses, and visible Previous / Pause / Next buttons plus arrow keys and Space make every gesture optional. Slides are typographic compositions drawn in CSS.
accessibility: Visible Previous, Pause/Play and Next buttons (WCAG 2.2.2 pause control and 2.5.1 single-pointer alternative to tap zones and press-and-hold).
The focusable story region answers ← and → (previous/next) and Space (pause/play); a text line always says "Slide n of N".
Slides are groups labelled "n of N"; hidden slides are inert. The slide region is aria-live="polite" only while not auto-advancing, so screen readers are not interrupted mid-story.
Tap zones and the progress segments are aria-hidden duplicates of the buttons; all copy is fictional sample content.
effects.reducedMotion: No auto-advance and no slide movement: the story waits for Previous/Next, segments show position statically and slides swap with a 160 ms fade.
performance: One WAAPI scaleX animation per visible segment drives both the bar and the advance (its finish event), so pausing is animation.pause() with no timers to resync.
Slide transitions are two short transform/opacity animations; every animation is cancelled on change and on unmount.

effects.name: SVG Path Draw
effects.description: An original line drawing of a lute assembles itself stroke by stroke: every path is normalised with pathLength="1", so one dash-offset keyframe draws any shape, and each part (body, rosette, frets, pegs, strings) gets its own easing on a single createSequence timeline before the fills arrive. Replay it, or scrub the timeline with a slider.
accessibility: The drawing is role="img" with <title> and <desc> describing the instrument; the individual strokes are not exposed.
Replay is a button and the scrubber is a native range input (arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End) with a "percent drawn" value text.
Scrubbing pauses playback, so the drawing only moves while the user is moving it.
effects.reducedMotion: The finished drawing is shown at once and Replay is a 160 ms fade; the scrubber still draws the lines, because that motion is under the user’s direct control.
performance: One WAAPI animation per path (stroke-dashoffset or fill-opacity) on a single createSequence timeline, so seek() scrubs everything with no per-frame JavaScript beyond the slider readout.
pathLength="1" means no getTotalLength() measuring and no layout reads.
The timeline is cancelled on unmount and rebuilt only when a parameter changes.

effects.name: Swipe Card Stack
effects.description: A shortlist deck you sort by flinging cards: the top card follows the pointer, tilts with the drag and is dismissed by distance or by release velocity, while the card beneath rises in step with the drag. Skip, Save and Undo buttons and the arrow keys do everything a swipe does.
accessibility: Every swipe has a single-pointer, non-dragging equivalent (WCAG 2.5.1 / 2.5.7): visible Skip, Save and Undo buttons of at least 44 px.
Left and Right arrows skip and save, Backspace or Z undoes, whenever focus is inside the deck; the top card is focusable and described by those instructions.
A polite live region announces each decision and how many cards remain; when a focused card leaves, focus moves to the next card (or to Start over).
Save and Skip are shown as words on the card and in the buttons, not by colour or direction alone; the stamps are decorative.
effects.reducedMotion: Cards no longer fly, tilt or rise: a decided card fades out in 160 ms and the next one is simply there. Dragging still moves the card under the finger because that movement is directly user-controlled.
performance: Drag, tilt, stamp opacity and the rise of the next card are motion values derived from one x value, so dragging causes no React renders.
Only the top card is draggable and only the visible slice of the deck is mounted.
Exit animations are springs seeded with the release velocity, so a flick carries its speed.

effects.name: Tilt Parallax Card
effects.description: A night-pass card that leans toward the pointer: sky, moon, hill and text sit on separate translateZ planes inside one preserve-3d card, so the tilt opens real parallax between them, while a soft specular highlight slides across the surface. The motion is a hand-rolled damped spring on the shared rAF loop that stops itself at rest; keyboard focus gives the card a gentle fixed tilt.
accessibility: The tilt is decorative and never carries information; the pass details are real text and the Save button is a normal toggle button (aria-pressed).
Keyboard focus inside the card (focus-visible) gives it a fixed, gentle tilt and highlight, so keyboard users see the same depth without a pointer.
Coarse pointers (touch) get no tilt, so scrolling past the card never wobbles it; artwork layers are aria-hidden.
effects.reducedMotion: No tilt, spring or moving highlight: the card rests flat with a fixed soft sheen, and focus shows only the standard focus ring.
performance: One damped spring per channel is integrated inside useRafLoop and written as CSS custom properties; React never re-renders while the card moves.
The loop runs only while the pointer is over the card or the spring is settling, and pauses offscreen or in a hidden tab.
Pointer position is measured on the untransformed wrapper, so the tilt cannot feed back into its own measurement; only transforms and one gradient change.

effects.name: Variable Weight Wave
effects.description: A headline whose variable-font weight (and optionally width) swells letter by letter under the pointer, breathes when idle and can be swept from the keyboard. Lines are locked after measuring so the block never reflows.
accessibility: The heading carries the sentence once through aria-label; every per-letter span and the measuring copy are aria-hidden.
The heading is focusable: keyboard focus sweeps the wave across the line and Arrow/Home/End keys move it letter by letter.
Text stays real DOM text and scales with zoom; weight never drops below the rest weight chosen for contrast.
effects.reducedMotion: The loop does not run: letters sit at a single mid weight and neither pointer, focus nor idle changes them.
performance: One rAF loop (useRafLoop, paused offscreen) writes a single custom property per letter and skips letters whose value did not change.
Letter centres are measured once per layout change, never inside the loop.
Lines are pre-measured and rendered nowrap, so weight changes cannot re-break lines or change the block height.

demos.name: Pulse Night Edition
demos.summary: An art-directed launch page: the Pulse speaker on a stone plinth in a dark room, an opening camera move you can skip, one key light shared by the scene and the copy, and a scroll-driven camera through two chapters, in which you can turn the speaker and its dial by hand.
highlights: Lens-shifted framing: each chapter sets the camera, the light and the speaker’s pose on its plinth so the speaker always stands opposite the copy, with no keystoning. Measured contrast of every copy block over the scene at each held chapter: 5.8:1 or better for body text.

One light for page and canvas: the key light and the generated environment swing towards the pointer through critically damped smoothing, the camera sways ±3°, and the same angle drives the headline’s sheen and the lit edges and shadows of the controls.

Hands on the subject: drag the speaker (or press ←/→ on the focused stage) and it turns on its plinth, keeps the release velocity and swings back on the heavy `glide` spring; in the dial chapter the same gesture turns the dial through 30 detents that snap on the quick `press` spring and drive the ring’s glow.

A staged opening: the rim light draws the silhouette, then the key comes up, then the ring glows, while the camera arcs in. Between chapters the camera swings and pulls back (01→02) or cranes up while the speaker turns half round on its plinth (02→03).
A filleted stone plinth whose sides fade into the dark, a two-layer contact shadow, a real key-light shadow where the profile allows shadow maps, and fog for depth.
accessibility: All copy is real text outside the canvas; the canvas has a name and a description of the scene, of what scrolling does and of what dragging does.

The focusable stage is the keyboard twin of the drag: ←/→ turn the speaker, and in the Dial chapter they turn the dial one detent each. Two buttons (Turn the dial down/up) do the same without a pointer; the volume is announced once the dial comes to rest.
The opening move has a Skip button; the light’s slow drift and the ring’s breathing have a Pause control (WCAG 2.2.2). Section buttons jump to each chapter.
Every copy block sits on a directional scrim (or, when stacked, a dark glass card), so contrast holds whatever the camera frames behind it.
Without WebGL, or if the model fails to load, a still render sits opposite the copy and the copy and the volume buttons are unchanged.
demos.reducedMotion: No opening move, no camera sway, no light drift or pointer light, no breathing ring: the camera and the speaker’s pose cut to each chapter. Dragging still turns the speaker and the dial under your hand, but they return or snap without springing; ←/→ hold the speaker turned while pressed.
performance: Continuous rendering only while the light plays and the stage is on screen; paused or under reduced motion it renders on demand: scroll, pointer, drag and settling springs request frames and stop when everything is at rest.

One model (the variant for the quality profile: 131k triangles on low-power), the plinth and one contact-shadow quad: about 16 draw calls. The plinth’s stone and the contact shadow are drawn once on 2D canvases (256 px and 512 × 256 px) and disposed on unmount.

Scroll and pointer are read through passive listeners into refs; React renders only when the chapter or the volume changes. The shared light reaches CSS as two custom properties written only when they change.

demos.name: Drift — a particle study
demos.summary: GPU-driven particles that form and re-form a sphere, a torus and an abstract glyph, pushed around by a pointer or a finger, with live renderer readouts that are measured, never invented.
highlights: All motion happens in the vertex shader: each particle stores its point on three forms plus a seed; the CPU only updates uniforms.
Morphs are staggered per particle and bloom outwards mid-flight; a pointer, a touch drag or the Pulse button disturbs the field.
The requested count is scaled by the quality profile (density 1 / 0.6 / 0.3) and the quality can be switched live, rebuilding the canvas.
The readout is renderer.info from the last frame; the only timing shown is the rAF interval, measured on this device and labelled as such.
accessibility: Every control is a native radio, checkbox, range, select or button with a visible label; the current form is also stated in text.
The pointer disturbance has a keyboard equivalent: the Pulse button sends the same kind of push through the field.
The continuous animation has a Pause control (WCAG 2.2.2); the canvas has a text description that follows the form and count.
Without WebGL a still SVG drawing of the sphere form replaces the canvas.
demos.reducedMotion: The field is a still frame rendered on demand: no flow, no automatic cycling, forms cut instead of morphing, and the pointer push and Pulse are off. Intensity, count, flow (which picks the frozen phase) and form still redraw the still.
performance: One draw call for the whole field; additive blending with depth writes off, so there is no sorting.
Count = requested × profile density; DPR is capped per profile. In headless SwiftShader the low profile renders 7,200 points.
Continuous loop only while the field animates and is on screen (StudioCanvas pauses offscreen); paused or reduced motion switches to render-on-demand.
Form buffers are generated once per count (seeded, deterministic) and the geometry is disposed when the count changes.

demos.name: Blockwerk Play Table
demos.summary: Rigid-body physics with Rapier: drag, throw and stack wooden blocks, tilt gravity, and watch the render loop go idle once everything is asleep — with a full keyboard path through a body list.
highlights: The Rapier chunk (WebAssembly included) is code-split with React.lazy and only fetched once the canvas starts; loading and failure states are shown.
Fixed 1/60 s timestep on a clamped clock, sleeping bodies, a 40-body cap that recycles the oldest, and removal of anything that falls out of the world.
Render on demand: Rapier requests frames only while a body is awake, so a settled table draws nothing — the page shows the frame counter stopping.
Drag is kinematic: the grabbed block follows the pointer on a camera-facing plane and is thrown with the pointer’s recent velocity on release.
accessibility: Every pointer action has a keyboard path: choose a body in the list (a native radio group), then Nudge left/right/away/toward, Lift, Drop or Remove.
Body state (resting, moving, held) is text in the list; additions, removals and recycling are announced in a polite live region.
